item.title: Evan Williams named NFC defensive player of the month
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Packers safety Evan Williams has been named NFC defensive player of the month for October.
item.content:encoded:
Packers safety Evan Williams has been named NFC defensive player of the month for October.

In his third season, Williams has helped elevate Green Bay’s defense this year. He had 41 total tackles with four passes defensed, two interceptions, a sack, and a fumble recovery last month.

According to the league, Williams is the third safety since 2000 to tally at least 40 tackles and three takeaways in a single month. He’s the first to accomplish the feat since 2011.

This is Williams’ first defensive player of the month award.

In eight games this season, Williams has totaled 71 tackles, two tackles for loss, four QB hits, six passes defensed, and two interceptions.

item.title: Malik Nabers named NFC offensive player of the month
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Giants receiver Malik Nabers had a strong October and now has been recognized for it.
item.content:encoded:
Giants receiver Malik Nabers had a strong October and now has been recognized for it.

The NFL named Nabers NFC offensive player of the month.

He had 36 catches for a league-high 509 yards with two touchdowns in October.

As noted by the league, Nabers was No. 2 with 36 receptions last month and was the only player to record at least 100 receiving yards in four games.

This is Nabers’ first career player of the month award.

In seven games this year, Nabers has caught 48 passes for 605 yards with two touchdowns.

item.title: Drake Maye is the AFC offensive player of the month
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye heard a lot of criticism in September, but it faded away in October.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots quarterback Drake Maye heard a lot of criticism in September, but it faded away in October.

After throwing six interceptions during a 1-2 start to the season, Maye guided the Patriots to a 3-1 mark last month. Maye threw multiple touchdowns in all four of New England's games, including four in the team's win over the Raiders.

He was 90-of-134 for 1,199 yards, 12 touchdowns and two interceptions in those games and he also ran 23 times for 129 yards and two more scores.

The NFL announced on Wednesday that they have named Maye the AFC offensive player of the month. It's the first time he has received the award.

item.title: Report: Vikings are trending toward starting Carson Wentz on Monday night
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The soft benching of Kyler Murray in favor of backup Carson Wentz could be coming on Monday night against the Bills.
item.content:encoded:
The soft benching of Kyler Murray in favor of backup Carson Wentz could be coming on Monday night against the Bills.

Officially, the Vikings say they're evaluating Murray's hamstring injury, not that they're evaluating whether Wentz is the quarterback who gives them a better chance to win. But Adam Schefter reported on ESPN today that the Vikings appear to be moving toward Wentz starting against the Bills. Which may have to do with both Murray's injury and Murray's ineffectiveness.

"His status for Monday night is, at best, up in the air, and it sounds like it is trending toward Carson Wentz starting on Monday night," Schefter said. "Everybody's watched the games. It looks like, right now, there is a question about the quarterback position, and how they're going to handle it. And Carson Wentz looks like he's in line to start Monday night, and you just have to wonder what's going to happen with the quarterback position."

Even against an injury-riddled Lions defense on Sunday, Murray struggled, and Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell appeared to lose faith in Murray, punting the ball away to the Lions with three minutes remaining in the fourth quarter rather than trusting Murray to convert a fourth-and-5.

After that punt, the Lions ran out the clock and Murray never touched the ball again. If Wentz starts on Monday night and plays well against the Bills, it might be a long time before Murray touches the ball again.

item.content:encoded:
Playing in Spain on Sunday, the Falcons held a full practice overseas on Thursday after staging a walk-through on Wednesday.

Notably, running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) remained limited on the report.

Robinson is No. 2 on the team with 211 rushing yards, behind league-leader Bijan Robinson, who has 780.

Linebacker Yasir Abdullah (hamstring) and linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) were also limited on Thursday.

Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), receiver Beaux Collins (hip), and offensive tackle Cameron Williams (ankle) were all full participants.

Receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring) did not practice as he’s already been ruled out for the Week 9 matchup.

item.title: Mike Evans is unlikely to play in Week 9
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: It is set to be another week without wide receiver Mike Evans for the 49ers.
item.content:encoded:
It is set to be another week without wide receiver Mike Evans for the 49ers.

Evans did not play in Week 7 due to Achilles tendinitis and he remained out for the team's first post-bye practice on Wednesday. General Manager John Lynch stopped short of ruling him out for Week 9's game against the Raiders during a Thursday appearance on KNBR, but said that it is "probably unlikely" that the wideout is back in action on Sunday.

Lynch referenced Christian McCaffrey's past issues with a similar injury and said the 49ers "don’t want it to become something that really lingers" for Evans because the goal is for him to be as impactful as he was in the early part of the season.

Deebo Samuel has been out since Week 5 with a hamstring injury and he was also out of Wednesday's practice.

The 49ers could get a couple of wideouts back this week, however. Demarcus Robinson has been designated for return from injured reserve and KhaDarel Hodge, who played in the first three games of the season, returned to the practice squad after being released in early October.

item.title: Some wonder whether the 49ers are in play for Jonathan Taylor
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As the trade deadline creeps closer, some think a high-profile team is lurking as to the biggest name that remains potentially available.
item.content:encoded:
As the trade deadline creeps closer, some think a high-profile team is lurking as to the biggest name that remains potentially available.

Chris Simms mentioned on Thursday's PFT Live that some in league circles are wondering whether the 49ers could make a play for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. (People around the league ask Simms those questions, because 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan is one of his best friends — and because they assume Simms knows what's happening with the 49ers, even if he rarely if ever does.)

A Taylor-to-49ers trade would be jarring. It would be unexpected. As jarring and unexpected as the news that emerged on a Thursday night in October 2022, when word first broke of the 49ers' trade with the Panthers for running back Christian McCaffrey.

A trade for Taylor would create obvious questions regarding McCaffrey. Taylor has $3.87 million remaining in base salary (after Week 9, it drops to $3.49 million). McCaffrey has a 2026 cap number of $10.861 million. While that's low enough to keep the duo together for the rest of the season, things would change in 2027.

McCaffrey has a cap number of $26.4 million, with no guaranteed money in what will be the last year of his current deal. Taylor would count for more than $16 million in 2027, under his current contract.

Most likely, the 49ers would move on from McCaffrey after this season, if they trade for Taylor.

And, yes, it would be a stunner if the 49ers trade for Taylor. The exact same kind of stunner that it was when the 49ers traded for McCaffrey in 2022.

But that's what teams do when they're serious about going all in. The Bears are. The Seahawks are. The 49ers may be.

Every contender needs to ask itself that question as the trade deadline approaches. Are you content to wish in one hand and shit in the other and see which one fills up first? Or are you going to turn a wishlist into tangible action items aimed at potentially putting a Super Bowl ring on everyone's finger?

item.title: PFT's Week 9 2026 NFL picks
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: A week after 13-1, here's hoping there won't be a 1-14 backslide.
item.content:encoded:
It all came down to Monday night.

Through Sunday, I'd somehow managed to go 13-0 in the Week 8 picks. The only thing standing in the way of unprecedented PFT perfection was Monday night — Bears at Seahawks.

And I'd picked the Seahawks.

I'll still take 13-1. And I'll keep trying to run the table.

For the year, I'm now 73-49-1. That's 59.3 percent for the year.

The goal this week? To not backslide to 1-14, with 30 teams playing and the Steelers and Titans off.

Jaguars at Ravens (Thursday night)

It's a short-week trap for the Jaguars, who managed to not fall into the Week 8 trap against the short-staffed Colts.

Jaguars 27, Ravens 13.

Bengals vs. Falcons (in Madrid)

The Falcons are way too inconsistent to trust in any given game, especially against a Bengals team that is clicking far more often than it isn't. Besides, the mini-Super Bowl vibe of an international game will likely push quarterback Joe Burrow to a playoff level of performance.

Bengals 27, Falcons 23.

Broncos at Panthers

It's a Super Bowl 50 rematch, between one team that is a Super Bowl contender and one team that is not.

Broncos 24, Panthers 16.

Cowboys at Colts

It's a Super Bowl V rematch, between one team that knows it's not a Super Bowl contender and one team that continues to delude itself.

Cowboys 27, Colts 17.

Jets at Chiefs

The Chiefs may play with their food (again) on Sunday, but they'll eventually eat the whole meal.

Chiefs 30, Jets 13.

Lions at Dolphins

The Dolphins should not be taken lightly. The Lions can't afford to do that, given the quality of the division they occupy.

Lions 24, Dolphins 10.

Browns at Saints

The Saints still have a chance to get things right, and they're desperate to avoid starting 0-4 in the Superdome.

Saints 23, Browns 14.

Giants at Eagles

It's suddenly the Bizarro NFC East, with the Giants in first place and the Eagles in the basement.

Giants 23, Eagles 13.

Rams at Commanders

The Rams have fully emerged from their early-season slump.

Rams 27, Commanders 19.

Texans at Chargers

There are some reasons for hope in Houston. There is no reason to expect any positive change from the Chargers, who continue to behave as if they're closer to 7-0 than 0-7.

Texans 21, Chargers 7.

Packers at Patriots

Did you hear Tom Brady is returning to Foxboro? (If you didn't, we envy you.) The Patriots need to keep pace with the Bills, and the Packers (while good) need Micah Parson back before they'll have a shot at being great.

Patriots 31, Packers 21.

Cardinals at Seahawks

If the Seahawks pick up a fifth loss before Veteran's Day, they'll almost definitely be sitting at home on Valentine's Day.

Seahawks 28, Cardinals 17.

Raiders at 49ers

In a renewal of a rivalry so intense that they had to stop playing each other in the preseason, the Raiders will make it interesting.

49ers 24, Raiders 20.

Buccaneers at Bears (Sunday night)

The Bucs have found their formula for winning, and they're in position to run away with the NFC South.

Bears 24, Buccaneers 21.

Bills at Vikings (Monday night)

Josh Allen is good enough to find the holes in the Minnesota defense before the rush can get to him. And the Vikings' offense isn't good enough to keep pace.

Bills 22, Vikings 17.

item.title: Sean McVay: I've coached Rams for 10 years, this is the worst for injuries to key players
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Rams head coach Sean McVay says he's never had to manage a team dealing with as many injuries to important players as this year's team.
item.content:encoded:
Rams head coach Sean McVay says he's never had to manage a team dealing with as many injuries to important players as this year's team.

McVay said on Wednesday that the only year comparable was 2022, when the defending Super Bowl champion Rams slumped to 5-12 thanks in large part to a spate of injuries. But this year, McVay says, has been even worse than that.

"I've been the coach for 10 years, and I know 2022 was a season that we had a lot of injuries, particularly at the offensive line, but this has been more than any year, including '22, with the amount of guys out at different spots that are key and critical to our identity, on offense, on defense and on special teams," McVay said.

The most recent injury McVay was discussing was the loss of cornerback Jaylen Watson, whom McVay praised as having had an outstanding season to this point, but has now been lost for the season with a shoulder injury. Other key players currently on injured reserve include defensive end Myles Garrett, wide receiver Davante Adams, defensive tackle Kobie Turner, tight end Terrance Ferguson, defensive tackle Poona Ford and kicker Blake Grupe.

Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford is also dealing with a sore arm, and although Stafford said he's going to be fine, he did acknowledge the Rams have been through a lot with injuries.

"That's just the way it goes. That's NFL football. I know everybody in that training room is doing everything they can to be back as fast as they can, and when and if those guys can do that, we'll welcome them with open arms and it'll be a nice boost for us when they get back," Stafford said.

After entering the season as the favorites to win the Super Bowl, the Rams are now 4-4. Getting healthy and staying healthy will be key to playing better over the second half of the season.

item.title: The Matthew Stafford elbow injury is a something to monitor
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: A question emerged about Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford's throwing arm after reporters spotted ice on it following Sunday's game against the Chargers.
item.content:encoded:
A question emerged about Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford's throwing arm after reporters spotted ice on it following Sunday's game against the Chargers. On Monday, coach Sean McVay called it "soreness" but otherwise deferred to Stafford for any specific questions.

On Wednesday, Stafford was asked specific questions.

“It feels good," Stafford said regarding what was described by the team as a right elbow injury on Wednesday. "Full practice as I have been all year and hope to continue to be that way.”

So why did he have an ice pack on his elbow when he left the locker room on Sunday?

“You guys have been blind," Stafford said with a laugh and a smile. "I feel like I've been icing my arm every day out here walking around. That's on you guys. You all are the ones that are out there reporting that I have ice on my arm. Listen, I'm 38 years old trying to keep up with these young bucks. A little bit of soreness and stuff that is not uncommon this time of year. Again, I haven’t missed a rep at practice. I haven’t missed a rep in a game and I feel good. I'm not too worried about it.”

As Simms pointed out on PFT Live, elbow soreness is uncommon at this stage of the season. Quarterbacks throw less during practice in the regular season. If soreness is going to happen, it's going to happen during training camp.

It's hard not to wonder whether the Rams disclosed Stafford as having an elbow specifically because someone finally noticed, and asked about, the ice (if, as Stafford claims, he has constantly been icing the elbow). If it's no big deal, why list the right elbow on the first injury report prior to the Week 9 game at Washington?

There are plenty of strategic reasons to not list an elbow issue. In 2019, the Steelers concealed quarterback Ben Roethlisberger's elbow problem. Then, in Week 2, he suffered a season-ending, non-contact elbow injury. The Steelers and coach Mike Tomlin eventually were fined, $75,000 and $25,000, respectively, for not disclosing the elbow issue.

As to Stafford, it's something to monitor. Especially since he's 38 and has thrown thousands of passes. Something in the elbow is bothering him.

And it could be affecting the number of pass plays the Rams are calling during games. After throwing for more than 50 passes in Week 3 (55), Week 4 (51), and Week 5 (54), he has thrown 33 in Week 6, 29 in Week 7, and 25 in Week 8.

While, for now, it's not impacting his ability to take his regular complement of practice snaps, it could be impacting his ability to generate maximum force and velocity on his throws. And, eventually, it could get worse.

Stafford has played through many injuries during his career. He'll play through this one, too. Unless and until he physically can't.

item.title: Shedeur Sanders deflects question about his decision to hire an agent
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Last month, Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders hired an agent for the first time.
item.content:encoded:
Last month, Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders hired an agent for the first time. It's a move that invites speculation and curiosity about the reason(s) for doing it, since Sanders won't be eligible for an adjustment to his contract until the conclusion of the 2027 regular season.

On Wednesday, Sanders spoke to reporters in his capacity as the tentative starter for Week 9, given that Deshaun Watson is in the concussion protocol. Sanders was asked about the decision to hire an agent.

“What’s that have to do with this game?” Sanders said. "I’m focused on this game. Anything else really doesn’t matter at this point.”

That's fine, but it was a fair question. Especially since the most reasonable conclusion is that he's thinking about engineering a trade.

Bolstering that perception is the fact that he hired an agent not long after receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. hired an agent — which resulted not long after that in a trade from the Cardinals to the Texans.

While a trade before next week's deadline is highly unlikely, Sanders could get an opportunity on Sunday to show the rest of the league what he can do. Which could spark trade interest in the offseason.

His performance also becomes a data point for the Browns, who will be making decisions about their own quarterback position after the current season ends. If Sanders thrives, the Browns could decide to give him a chance to be the starter next year, if they don't re-sign Watson.

item.title: Josh Jacobs: "There's a lot of stuff being said about me that's completely false"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Friday, Wisconsin authorities released documents in the Josh Jacobs criminal case that included three allegations against him from other women.
item.content:encoded:
On Friday, Wisconsin authorities released documents in the Josh Jacobs criminal case that included three allegations against him from other women. On Wednesday, Jacobs spoke directly to reporters for the first time since the material became public.

"It's one of those things for me where it's like, it really feels like an attack on me and who I am and my character," Jacobs said, via Rob Demovsky of ESPN. "And at the end of the day, there's a lot of stuff being said about me that's completely false -- like, completely made up, and it's like people just run with it. And I can't change that.

"It's just one of those things where it's like, OK, all I can do is try to be who I am and try not to let the negative moments change who I am. And that was the biggest thing for me throughout this whole process. I didn't want to go to a place where I felt like I was closed off and I'm angry all the time because of what's going on in my life."

The situation would be very different if Jacobs hadn't pleaded no contest to a misdemeanor battery charge arising from an incident in May 2026. Admitting to an incident of violence against a woman makes it harder for him to credibly claim that three other women who contacted authorities about Jacobs doing the same thing are making it all up.

Still, Jacobs believes the newly-surfaced allegations won't result in more missed time, following the six-game stint on paid leave arising from the most recent incident.

"With all the evidence that we have and that they have at this point, it's not one of those things where I'm sitting back on my hands like, 'OK, am I going to play this week?'" Jacobs said. "It's like, I kind of already know what it is, so it's like . . . it's really just up to them to make their final decision. But like I'm not worried about feeling like I'm going to miss any more time than I already have."

The league continues to investigate Jacobs, and it's investigating the recent allegations, too. Through it all, the Packers have been linked on multiple occasions to a potential trade for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. If the Packers land Taylor, it could mean that they'll move on from Jacobs.

item.title: Jack Campbell: I have full movement in my lower body, and am making progress with movement in my upper body
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Lions released a statement from Campbell on Wednesday providing an update on his condition after he suffered a significant neck injury on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Lions linebacker Jack Campbell has issued a statement on Wednesday after suffering a serious neck injury on Sunday, saying that he has full movement in his lower body and is continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body.

This is the first definitive update on Campbell's condition since he was transported to the hospital on Sunday.

"I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time," Campbell's statement reads, in part. "I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better."

Campbell went on to thank those who have helped take care of him since Sunday.

“I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field,” Campbell said. "I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you.

“I also can’t say enough about the incredible care I’ve received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They’ve been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I’m truly grateful for everything they’ve done.”

Campbell added, “To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I’m proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn’t ask to be surrounded by a better group of people.

“One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge.

“Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can’t thank everyone enough.”

item.content:encoded:
The Vikings have let go of an offensive lineman.

Minnesota announced on Tuesday that the club has waived guard Trevor Keegan.

Keegan, 26, appeared in seven games for Minnesota this season. He was on the field for 30 special teams snaps and three offensive snaps.

The Vikings had claimed Keegan off waivers in September. An Eagles fifth-round pick in 2024, Keegan has also spent time with the Cowboys.

Additionally, Minnesota has released tight end Bryson Nesbit from its practice squad.

item.title: Micah Parsons expects "All-Pro" moments and "terrible" moments once he's back in games
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Packers defensive end Micah Parsons isn't willing to pinpoint a date for his return to game action, but it is on everyone's mind now that he is back on the practice field.
item.content:encoded:
Packers defensive end Micah Parsons isn't willing to pinpoint a date for his return to game action, but it is on everyone's mind now that he is back on the practice field.

Parsons did individual work in his practice return on Wednesday and said that expects to do even more during next week's workouts. Recent reports have Week 12 circled as the likeliest time for Parsons to make his 2026 debut and he discussed his expectations for that moment with reporters after his first practice session.

When asked if it's realistic for him to play at an All-Pro level right out of the gate, Parsons said that it was but added that he expects to "have terrible plays" as well due to how much rest accumulated during his recovery from last December's torn ACL.

“Am I gonna go out there and play 50, 60 snaps, how I was doing before? Absolutely not. It’s just not realistic," Parsons said. "My body’s not there yet. I don’t even think my knee is built for that yet. I didn’t go through a training camp. Am I going to be the All-Pro Micah, the person I once was this year? Probably not until later, after I go through all my phases and things like that. . . . I think you'll see flashes of All-Pro Micah when I get to pass rush, and there's going to be times when you're going to be like, 'Dang, what was Micah doing?' There's going to be times when I question myself, too. Like, what was I doing right there? I'm not ashamed of that. I'm not scared of seeing the failure of this thing because I just came back from 11-month injury. I’m not shying away from the possibility of bad plays."

It's an honest appraisal of what the return from a long layoff is likely to look like, but a big play or two from Parsons can help swing a game and the Packers would gladly sign up for that while waiting for the total package to come back together.

item.title: Report: Eagles to start Joe Milton at QB this week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said on Monday that the team would not be making a quarterback change for their Week 9 game against the Giants, but it appears he has changed his mind.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said on Monday that the team would not be making a quarterback change for their Week 9 game against the Giants, but it appears he has changed his mind.

ESPN reports that Joe Milton will get the start this week. Tanner McKee has started all three games since Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve and the Eagles have lost all three of those contests.

Milton was signed off the Cowboys' practice squad when Hurts was placed on injured reserve. He has not appeared in a game for the Eagles, but made five appearances for the Patriots and Cowboys over the last two seasons. He was 37-of-53 for 424 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while also running 15 times for 66 yards and a score.

Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio called the trade that landed this week's opposing quarterback J.J. McCarthy a "steal" for the Giants and the Eagles will look for a similar offensive jolt from Milton when the NFC East teams face off this week.

item.title: Will Anderson Jr.: Justin Herbert is playing out of his mind
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: It's been a rough 2026 for the Chargers, who are now 0-7 after last Sunday's loss to the Rams.
item.content:encoded:
It's been a rough 2026 for the Chargers, who are now 0-7 after last Sunday's loss to the Rams.

But one member of the team's next opponent sees strong play from quarterback Justin Herbert.

Texans defensive end Will Anderson complimented the signal-caller for his play when talking to reporters on Wednesday.

"He's still a really great quarterback in this league,” Anderson said, via transcript from the team. “You talk about a big guy that has a big arm that can run around, that can throw the ball deep, makes a lot of plays with his legs. He's still a very respectable player in this league and we have a ton of respect for them. As far as scheme, we're going to probably see a lot of bounce. [Chargers OC Mike] McDaniel, he's went against this defense a lot of times, coached against his defense at San Fran.

“We know what to expect a little bit, but Herbert, he's playing out of his mind. They have a really great solid offensive line as well and some really good running backs that can get downhill, that can hit the perimeter, it's going to be a good challenge for us.”

Whether one agrees with Anderson’s assessment is in the eye of the beholder. But Herbert has completed 61.8 percent of his passes for 1,398 yards with five touchdowns and a league-leading 10 interceptions in 2026.

item.title: Jaguars' defense aiming for 25th straight game not allowing a 75-yard rusher
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Down to their third-string quarterback, the Ravens will likely need a big game from Derrick Henry.
item.content:encoded:
With the Ravens down to their third-string quarterback on Thursday night against the Jaguars, Baltimore will rely heavily on running back Derrick Henry. Unfortunately for the Ravens, it's been a long time since a running back has had a big game against the Jaguars' defense.

The Jaguars haven't allowed an opposing runner to gain 75 or more yards in a game in the last 24 games. If the Jaguars don't allow a 75-yard runner against the Ravens on Thursday night, they will become just the third team in the Super Bowl era to go 25 straight games without allowing an opposing runner to gain 75 yards.

Henry is leading the NFL with 158 rushing attempts this season, and he may very well get the ball even more than 20 times per game he's averaging so far this season. Undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano is making the first start of his career for the Ravens, so they're likely to need to get a big game running the ball if they're going to pull off the upset over the Jaguars.

Although Henry is still carrying the ball a lot at the age of 32, his effectiveness has waned. He's averaging a career-low 4.0 yards per carry. It won't be easy to have a breakout game against the Jaguars, but the Ravens need him to do it.

item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts made an appearance at the team's practice facility on Wednesday, Tim McManus of ESPN reports.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts made an appearance at the team's practice facility on Wednesday, Tim McManus of ESPN reports.

It is the first time some players had seen Hurts since he went on injured reserve with blood clots in his lungs.

Hurts sat in on the team meeting and additional meetings, but he did not address the team.

Coach Nick Sirianni did not address a question Wednesday about whether the quarterback had been at the facility.

"I've talked to him and am in constant communication with him and know he's resting and recovering," Sirianni said. "I miss him like crazy. But nothing new on that front. I know he's resting and recovering, and we're all still praying for him and hoping for a speedy recovery."

Hurts, 28, went on injured reserve on Oct. 17 and is expected to miss the rest of the season.

Tanner McKee went 0-3 in Hurts' absence before being benched for Joe Milton this week.

item.title: Christian McCaffrey says "I feel great" after hamstring injury, but he didn't practice on Wednesday
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Thigh injury that became hamstring problem keeps McCaffrey out of practice.
item.content:encoded:
49ers running back Christian McCaffrey missed part of the Week 7 loss to the Falcons with what had been called a thigh injury during the game. By Monday, it had been revised to a hamstring injury.

Nine days later, McCaffrey wasn't able to practice because of it.

In the first official injury report issued by the 49ers since they said he had a thigh injury during the Week 7 loss, the 49ers say that McCaffrey missed practice due to a hamstring injury.

After the game in Atlanta, McCaffrey said it felt like his leg "just died on me." On Wednesday, McCaffrey expressed optimism that he'll play on Sunday against the Raiders.

“I had no idea [it was a hamstring injury],” McCaffrey said Wednesday, via Vic Tafur of The Athletic. “Sometimes the adrenaline and all these other things can get to you. . . . It wasn’t too bad. Having the bye week was awesome. But now I feel great.”

Still, not great enough to practice. Which creates the kind of mixed signals that conjure memories of the strange way in which the team handled McCaffrey's 2024 Achilles injury, which resulted in his unexpected scratch for the regular-season opener.

Here's the basic reality. He had a career-high 413 touches in 2025. He has 118 in seven games this year. Now 30, the workload can take a toll — especially in a 17-game season.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan: Nothing's changed for me with Brandon Aiyuk, I've moved on mentally
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: When 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan was asked in September if the team's injury issues at wide receiver had led him to consider bringing Brandon Aiyuk back, his answer was a strong no.
item.content:encoded:
When 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan was asked in September if the team's injury issues at wide receiver had led him to consider bringing Brandon Aiyuk back, his answer was a strong no.

Aiyuk has started the process of being reinstated from the team's reserve/left squad list and part of that process would involve him reporting to the team's facility later this week if he has not been released ahead of time. Shanahan was asked at a Wednesday press conference about any expectations he has about such a visit.

“None. I have no expectation," Shanahan said. "I’ve kind of moved on with that mentally and doing kind of how I talked to you guys two months ago. Nothing’s really changed for me.”

Shanahan said he has not had any conversations about a roster exemption that would give the 49ers more time to explore a trade, which joins releasing him or welcoming him back to the active roster as the team's options once he is off the left squad list. Shanahan said there are "no absolutes" when asked if he could envision any scenario where Aiyuk plays for the team again, but his other answers sent a strong message that Aiyuk will be moving on once the administrative work is done.

item.title: Todd Monken: Deshaun Watson not ruled out yet, but Shedeur Sanders preparing to start
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson is in the concussion protocol after self-reporting symptoms on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson is in the concussion protocol after self-reporting symptoms on Tuesday.

Head coach Todd Monken told reporters in his Wednesday press conference that Watson hasn’t necessarily been ruled out for Sunday’s game against New Orleans. But the club is preparing Shedeur Sanders to start.

“What I would say is, credit to Deshaun — after the game, [he] felt fine. Monday night, started feeling a little bit, little bit of a headache, and came in Tuesday and, you know, reported,” Monken said, via transcript from the team. “So, credit to him for someone who really loves playing the game. And so, he is in the protocol. And Shedeur will take the reps today with the ones.”

Monken admitted that it’s “a little more difficult” for a quarterback to play on Sunday after missing practice due to a concussion. But Monken and the team will let the process play out.

“I mean, there’s a long time between now and then, right? I mean, look where the Ravens are at. And you don’t know as the week goes on what could happen,” Monken said. “It’s not ideal, right? It’s not ideal for any player to go through a week and not practice and then play. We know that. But every situation is different.”

Monken noted that Watson can participate in the team’s meetings to help him stay prepared in the event that he gets cleared. The team has been game-planning with the idea that Sanders will start. But Monken said the game plan won’t change much if it’s Sanders or Watson behind center.

“I don’t see the way [it would change], because the rest of the guys are the same, and they’re similar in some ways,” Monken said. “Some things, you know, Shedeur’s skill set is different than Deshaun’s, but still very similar in terms of what we do. We can’t change that dramatically.”

Either way, Watson is expected to still be the starter when he is cleared.

“Yeah, I didn’t assume I’d get that question. Yeah, he’s been our starter for eight games. I would assume he’s still our starter,” Monken said. “I don’t — I’m thinking about Wednesday. But I’m not — I’m really thinking about today and watching Shedeur play today.”

So far this season, Watson has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards with seven touchdowns and three interceptions. He’s been sacked a league-high 33 times. His eight games this season are the most he’s played in a year for the Browns since arriving on the club in 2022.

Last season, Sanders completed 56.6 percent of his throws for 1,400 yards with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions in eight games with seven starts.

item.title: Report: Ravens finalizing trade for Jacoby Brissett
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Brissett is on his way to Baltimore after being benched by the Cardinals.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens will be starting Joe Fagnano at quarterback against the Jaguars on Thursday night, but it looks like they will have a more experienced option available for Week 10 and beyond.

ESPN reports that they are finalizing a trade with the Cardinals for Jacoby Brissett. The deal will not be done by Thursday night's game, but it is expected to be completed over the weekend.

Brissett started the first eight games of the season for Arizona, but was benched in favor of Gardner Minshew last Sunday and demoted to the No. 3 spot on the depth chart this week. Brissett signed a revised contract with the Cardinals after a protracted absence from the team this offseason, but most of the money has been paid out already and the Ravens will be responsible for the remainder of his base salary.

The move to No. 3 made Brissett an obvious trade candidate and the Ravens were a logical destination. Lamar Jackson could be out for the rest of the season with a thumb injury and Tyler Huntley will miss the rest of the year with turf toe, which left the undrafted Fagnano and other inexperienced players as the in-house options for Baltimore.

item.title: Matthew Stafford has full participation with elbow injury; Myles Garrett limited in return
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Rams coach Sean McVay wouldn't allow much about the ice pack on quarterback Matthew Stafford's arm after Sunday's win over the Chargers other than to say it was soreness.
item.content:encoded:
Rams coach Sean McVay wouldn’t allow much about the ice pack on quarterback Matthew Stafford's arm after Sunday's win over the Chargers other than to say it was soreness. The injury report said it isn't serious, and Stafford agreed.

Stafford was a full participant, listed with an elbow injury.

"I’m 38 years old, trying to keep up with these young bucks. Little bit of soreness and stuff that is not uncommon this time of year," Stafford said, via Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times. "Haven't missed a rep. Feel good. So I'm not too worried about it."

Stafford underwent surgery on his elbow during the 2022 offseason.

He threw only 25 passes on Sunday.

The Rams got more good news when outside linebacker Myles Garrett (knee) returned to practice as a limited participant. It was the first practice Garrett and Aaron Donald have had together.

Garrett underwent arthroscopic knee surgery in mid-September after playing 40 snaps in the season opener. He was given a six-week prognosis and has missed seven games.

The Rams practiced without cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder), long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle), cornerback Trent McDuffie (back), tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs) and safety Kam Curl (foot) on Wednesday.

Inside linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), offensive lineman Steve Avila (hamstring), wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back) and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle) were limited.

item.title: Sam Darnold out Week 9 with quad injury, Drew Lock in line to start
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: HC Mike Macdonald said Darnold also suffered a cracked rib early in Monday's loss to the Bears.
item.content:encoded:
Seattle's QB1 for Week 9 is in flux.

Quarterback Sam Darnold will not play in Sunday's game against the Cardinals after suffering a quad injury late in Monday's loss to the Bears, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald announced in his Wednesday press conference.

"It’ll be week-to-week for Sam," Macdonald said. "He’s not going to go on IR."

Macdonald noted the club intends to start Drew Lock on Sunday, but he's also working through an injury.

"The plan is for Drew to start. Jalen [Milroe] will be ready to back up," Macdonald said. "Drew’s still working back from his elbow, so we’ll work through that process this week. So we’ll be getting both guys ready to play. Have full confidence in those guys and we have a plan in place and we’ll go execute."

Lock finished the Week 1 win over the Patriots and started Week 2 when the Seahawks beat the Cardinals in Arizona. He’s completed 35-of-48 passes this year for 422 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions.

“He’s able to throw. How much, we’re working through that right now. That’s the best way to put it,” Macdonald said of Lock’s elbow injury. “He’s going to throw the ball throughout the week, but we’re just going to manage it. He’s not going to take 8,000 throws.”

Lock and Milroe are set to split reps at least early in the practice week.

“I think we just have to take it day-by-day at this point,” Macdonald said.

While Macdonald characterized Darnold as week-to-week with the quad injury, the quarterback is also dealing with another issue.

“In terms of Sam, this guy, he’s tough as nails,” Macdonald said. “I think the second play of the game, I just asked if I could share this, but he cracked his rib on the second play of the game. So, playing the whole game without even making a name of it, and playing his tail off, and competing, it’s worth noting how tough this guy is. He’ll be back sooner than later, I’m sure.”

Darnold has completed 60.2 percent of his passes this season for 1,478 yards with 10 touchdowns and nine interceptions so far this season.

Seattle’s first injury report of the week will be out later on Wednesday.

item.title: Nick Sirianni: I've always felt complete support from Jeffrey Lurie
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Nick Sirianni has never missed the playoffs since becoming the Eagles' head coach and he's won one of the two Super Bowls the team has played in during his tenure, but the waters have gotten rockier for him over the last 12 months.
item.content:encoded:
Nick Sirianni has never missed the playoffs since becoming the Eagles' head coach and he's won one of the two Super Bowls the team has played in during his tenure, but the waters have gotten rockier for him over the last 12 months.

The Eagles will bring a six-game losing streak into Sunday's game against the Giants and the team is 5-11 since an 8-2 start to the 2025 season. While his overall history and the overall circumstances of this season would say that he's earned a chance to turn things around, Eagles history says that team owner Jeffrey Lurie hasn't shied away from making changes after a season goes awry.

Doug Pederson also won a Super Bowl for the Eagles, but was dismissed after snapping a three-year postseason run by going 4-11-1 in 2020. That may have factored into a question for Sirianni on Wednesday about his communications with Lurie during the team's current difficulties.

"I've always felt nothing but complete support from Mr. Lurie in everything, through good times, through bad times," Sirianni said, via a transcript from the team. "That's huge. That's huge to be able to know that the owner has your back in all situations. We've been high of highs, we've been low, and I've felt nothing but support and my communication remains the same with him as it has [been] whether we're on a winning streak or whether we're on a losing streak. I love that steadiness, and I'm trying to give that same thing to the guys: the consistency, the steadiness, because I know I'm receiving it from the very top."

Sirianni spoke before word broke that the Eagles will veer away from steadiness at quarterback this week. They'll give Joe Milton a chance to run the offense well enough to snap a skid that will certainly impact Sirianni's job security if it doesn't come to an end relatively soon.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Saints can use all the help they can get after a 2-5 start to the season and one ray of hope is the return of rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson to the practice field this week.
item.content:encoded:
The Saints can use all the help they can get after a 2-5 start to the season and one ray of hope is the return of rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson to the practice field this week.

Tyson has been out since injuring his hamstring during a joint practice with the Jaguars in August, but the first-round pick was designated for return from injured reserve this week and he gave a very positive assessment of his health while speaking with reporters on Wednesday.

“I ran the fastest I ran since I been here in rehab. I feel more explosive than I ever have," Tyson said. "So I think I'm doing pretty good. I think I'm doing just fine."

The Saints haven't said if Tyson will play against the Browns this Sunday, but he said he's "pretty anxious" to make his NFL debut and start providing the big plays that the team envisioned when they took him eighth overall in April. That would be a positive way to head into the second half of a season that has not gone as hoped in New Orleans.

item.title: Lamar Jackson's latest injury raises obvious questions about his future in Baltimore
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Ravens wanted to re-sign him in 2026, and there's no reason to think they won't want to in 2027.
item.content:encoded:
With quarterback Lamar Jackson's ninth NFL season possibly over after three full games and two first-half exits, obvious questions have emerged regarding his future in Baltimore.

The facts fuel the speculation. He's under contract for one more season, and the Ravens can't use the franchise tag or the transition tag to limit his ability to become an unrestricted free agent in March 2028, which is only 16 months away.

If Jackson wants a fresh start at age 31, he'll be able to have one.

The Ravens made it clear in January that they wanted to extend his contract by the start of the new league year in March 2026. It didn't happen, for reasons that never became clear because neither Jackson nor the Ravens (at Jackson's behest) share information about the negotiations.

Before the season began, it seemed that a new contract wa just a matter of time. The Ravens surely would like to do it before the start of the new league year in March, when Jackson's cap number spikes to $84.34 million. Although the team has the right to do another restructuring that would reduce the 2027 cap number, that would make the dead-cap reckoning even larger as of 2028.

A trade would avoid the final $52 million in cash and cap charges, but the cap realities would make a post-June 1 move the far better option. And there have been whispers of at least one team doing advance homework on a potential pursuit of Jackson in 2027.

The overriding question is whether Jackson's lingering availability issue changes things for the Ravens. For now, there's no reason to think it has. When the dust settles on the season, the Ravens will have to revisit that question.

But that will lead to another question. What would they do at quarterback without Lamar Jackson? That simple reality prompted them to give him a market-level deal in 2023, and to want to do it again.

As long as that desire to avoid a future without Lamar Jackson remains, there's no reason to think he won't be back in Baltimore in 2027.

item.title: Broncos proactively replace entire surface at Mile High Stadium, again
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: With four regular-season home games played and four to go, the Broncos are being proactive — again — about the quality of the playing surface at Mile High Stadium.
item.content:encoded:
With four regular-season home games played and four to go, the Broncos are being proactive — again — about the quality of the playing surface at Mile High Stadium.

The entire field is being ripped up and replaced, despite the absence of any complaints about the quality of the grass there.

For the fifth straight year, the Broncos are spending the money to ensure that the players will be performing on the highest-quality surface, emphasizing that "the Walton Penner Family Ownership Group’s commitment to player safety and a best-in-class playing surface throughout the season."

At a time when the debate regarding real grass vs. fake grass continues, with the situation boiling down to whether the owners are willing to write the check to ensure the best and safest surfaces for players, the statement made by the Broncos makes their ownership look good and, in comparison, owners who cling to artificial turf look bad.

Beyond caring about player safety, having the best playing surface provides the best protection of the investment the owners have made in their rosters. Which would be a sensible position for any owner — especially the cheap ones.

Now that it has morphed into a matter of collective bargaining, those who choose to be pennywise have even more cover for their pound foolishness. Which makes it even more important that the NFL Players Association apply not general public pressure to the league but specific scrutiny to the owners who won't ditch artificial turf for grass, or who won't replace low-quality grass with high-quality grass.

item.title: Sean Payton says J.K. Dobbins remains "a huge part of what we're doing"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: It's been a somewhat strange second year in Denver for veteran running back J.K.
item.content:encoded:
It's been a somewhat strange second year in Denver for veteran running back J.K. Dobbins. As coach Sean Payton tells it, however, everything is going as planned.

“He’s a huge part of what we’re doing," Payton told reporters on Wednesday regarding whether the team is managing Dobbins's workload. "So each week we look at — a lot of times who’s the back that’s in there with the hot hand. But he’s been fantastic. So to answer your question: No, that’s not a hot button topic with us here. It might be with you guys, but not with us. So we’re good. We’re good with the rotation.”

Payton is generally using a three-back rotation, with Dobbins joining R.J. Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman. Still, with Harvey on injured reserve for Sunday's showdown against the Chiefs, Dobbins got fewer chances than Coleman.

Coleman, who was on the field for 41 offensive plays, had 11 carries for 41 yards and four catches for 63. Dobbins played 13 snaps, getting seven carries for 13 yards and no targets in the passing game.

"Look, it’s always easy to work two [running backs] and it becomes more challenging when you’re trying to work three, but he’s doing a great job," Payton said of Dobbins.

For the year, Dobbins has 94 carries for 306 yards in eight games, with eight catches for 27 yards. That's 333 yards from scrimmage — an average of 41.6 per game.

In 10 games last year, before he suffered a season-ending foot injury during a Thursday night game against the Raiders, Dobbins was averaging nearly twice that amount, at 80.9 yards from scrimmage per game.

Through it all, the Broncos have been linked to a potential trade for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. While the prospect of acquiring a workhorse would cut against Payton's longstanding approach to use multiple running backs, Taylor's arrival would surely result in even fewer chances for Dobbins.
